title: Interview with Sweta Gupta, VP of Engineering of Analog Bits
gist: Analog Bits VP of Engineering Sweta Gupta says customers' biggest challenge at sub-3nm nodes (TSMC N3P, N2P, A14) is power integrity, thermal hotspots and precise clocking driven by AI workloads and chiplets. Analog Bits differentiates by silicon-validating its PLL, SerDes, sensor and power-management IP on its own test chips across TSMC, Samsung, Intel and GlobalFoundries, and is investing in on-die power telemetry, thermal sensing for 3D stacks and pinless clocking.

insights.claim: Sweta Gupta says customers' biggest challenge today is managing power integrity, thermal runaway and precise clocking at advanced sub-3nm nodes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power/thermal management IP demand rises with AI chip complexity.
insights.quote: The biggest challenge our customers face today is managing power integrity, thermal runaway, and precise clocking at advanced sub-3nm nodes.

insights.claim: AI workloads, multi-die chiplets and high-density data centers cause severe localized voltage droops from sudden current spikes and unpredictable thermal hotspots that threaten chip lifetime and performance in advanced multicore SoCs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: On-die sensing and power management become critical IP categories for AI chips.

insights.claim: Taping out on leading-edge processes like TSMC N3P, N2P or the upcoming A14 is a massive financial risk if mixed-signal IP fails to behave predictably under extreme conditions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rising tapeout costs increase value of pre-validated silicon IP.

insights.claim: Analog Bits validates IP in silicon by taping out its own test chips with PLLs, SerDes, sensors and power management IP, characterized across PVT extremes, on TSMC, Samsung, Intel and GlobalFoundries FinFET and GAA nodes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Multi-foundry silicon validation is a moat for analog IP vendors.
insights.quote: We carry that risk before our customers have to, so what they integrate has already been measured on silicon at their node.

insights.claim: Developing complex mixed-signal IP in-house requires specialized expertise, investment and time, diverting resources and extending time to market, so even the largest ASIC suppliers with internal analog teams view Analog Bits as a partner.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supports the outsourced analog IP model even against in-house teams.

insights.claim: Analog Bits has shifted from compact wide-range PLLs two decades ago to creating numerous power monitoring and controlling IPs to address power delivery issues in modern high-power, low-voltage chips.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power-management IP is the growth vector for analog IP vendors.

insights.claim: Analog Bits sees three near-term customer challenges: energy-efficient compute requiring on-die power sensors and telemetry, 3D stacking where thermal problems compound, and milliwatt-budget edge devices.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Maps where analog/mixed-signal IP demand will grow.

insights.claim: Thermal problems compound when dies are stacked, pushing Analog Bits to drive sensor accuracy and responsiveness to physical limits.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: 3D stacking raises demand for high-accuracy thermal sensors.
insights.quote: Thermal problems compound when dies are stacked

insights.claim: Analog Bits is leading on pinless technology and integrated high-performance clocking to reduce pin count and board-level dependencies for chiplet designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pinless IP addresses I/O constraints in chiplet integration.

insights.claim: Almost every advanced-node Analog Bits customer is building for AI, in data centers and HPC, at the edge, or in automotive, so its roadmap is shaped by AI needs for power, thermal management and high-speed clocking.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI dominates advanced-node demand even for analog IP suppliers.
insights.quote: Almost every advanced-node customer is building for AI
insights.locator: AI changed who our customers are

insights.claim: Analog Bits is adopting AI internally across engineering, QA and customer support to speed design iteration and verification and scale team coverage.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Internal AI adoption in IP vendors may improve margins/throughput.
insights.locator: AI changed who our customers are
